Action Plan:
1. Acute diarrheal illness – provide conservative management (oral re-hydration solution such as Dioralyte, maintain adequate fluid intake, light diet); symptomatic relief with paracetamol 1 g (two tablets) up to four times daily as needed for fever or pain; advise 2-3 days off work to rest and reduce spread of infection.
2. Safety-netting – patient to return or seek urgent care if symptoms persist beyond 3–4 days, worsen (e.g., bloody stools, ongoing vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, high fever), or new concerning features develop; potential stool culture may be arranged at review.
3. Asthma – continue usual inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); no change required.
4. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: 3-day history of loose, watery diarrhea (≈6–7 times/day).  
• Associated symptoms: intermittent cramp-like left lower abdominal pain, initial vomiting (now resolved), subjective fever at onset, weakness/shakiness, loss of appetite; no blood in stools or vomit.  
• Possible trigger: Chinese takeaway meal 4 days ago. One child had isolated vomiting; no similar diarrhea in household.  
• Past medical history: asthma (well-controlled). No known bowel disease.  
• Medications: asthma inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented); no others.  
• Allergies: not discussed.  
• Social history: married, lives with wife and two children; works as an accountant; non-smoker; does not consume alcohol.  

Objective:
• No physical examination or vital signs documented during this consult.  
• No investigations performed at this visit.  

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhea / suspected viral gastroenteritis  
   - Assessment: Likely viral gastroenteritis; bacterial etiology less likely but possible.  
   - Differential diagnosis: Food-borne bacterial gastroenteritis, inflammatory bowel disease flare (less likely).  
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; stool sample for culture if no improvement in 3–4 days.  
   - Treatment planned: Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) as directed; maintain fluid intake; light/soft diet; paracetamol 1 g up to QID PRN for fever/pain; rest for 2–3 days away from work.  
   - Safety net: Return for review or seek urgent care if symptoms persist >3–4 days, worsen, or new red-flag symptoms (blood in stool, persistent vomiting, high fever, signs of dehydration) occur.

2. Asthma (stable)  
   - Assessment: Well-controlled.  
   - Treatment planned: Continue current inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
   - No additional investigations or referrals needed at this time.

Quality checks:
● Missing information: Allergies, detailed medication name/dose/frequency for asthma inhaler, recent vital signs, objective abdominal examination.  
● No internal conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality adequate; occasional minor interruptions but clinically relevant details clear.
